lawyer:
Khan Saifur Rahman, Advocate ----- For the Petitioner.
A Baset Mojumder, Advocate ----- For Opposite Party.
parties:
Lutfur Rahman and others ----- Petitioners. 
Vs.
Mosammat Aleya Begum and others ----- Opposite Parties.
full_judgment:
Habibur Rahman Khan, J. : On an application filed under section 439 of the Criminal Procedure Code by Lutfor Rahman and 12 others a rule was issued by this Court on 7.1.91 calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned order dated 28.10.90 passed by Mr. Habibur Rahman Talukder, Sessions Judge, Dhaka in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2460 of 1989 under section 526(B) of the Code of Criminal Procedure should not be set aside. On the prayer of the petitioners the further proceedings of Sessions Case No. 162 of 1989 pending in the court of Additional Sessions Judge, Second Court, Dhaka and the Demra P.S Case No. 49(5)89 pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka were stayed pending the disposal of the Rule. 

 2. Two cases are pending for trial before the two different courts, one being Sessions Case No. 162 of 1989 under sections 148/149/307 of the Penal Code arising out of Demra PS Case No. 45(5) 89 (CR Case No. 1545/89) in which Haji Afsar Karim and others are accused, is pending before the Additional Sessions Judge, Second Court, Dhaka for trial and another arising out of Demra PS Case No. 49(5) 89 being GR Case No. 1549/89 under sections 148/149/307/327/306/380/109 of the Penal Code is pending for trial before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. While both the cases were ready for trial an application under section 526(B) of the Criminal Procedure Code was filed by Mst. Aleya Begum, the complainant of the Demra PS Case No. 49(5) 89 being Criminal Misc. Case No 2460 of 1989, with a prayer for simultaneous hearing of the case with the Sessions Case No. 162 of 1989 which arose out of Demra PS Case No. 45(5) 89 on the ground that both the cases arose out of the same occurrence and the parties are almost the same. The learned Sessions Judge by his judgment and order dated 28.10.90 withdrew the subsequent case being Demra PS Case No. 49(5) 89 from the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka to his own file holding that the case was a counter case of the earlier case being Demra PS Case No. 45(5) 89. The order dated 28.10.90 passed by the learned Sessions Judge Dhaka in Criminal Misc. Case No. 2460 of 1989 is now under challenge. 

 3. The learned Sessions Judge by his order dated 28.10.90 thus allowed the prayer of the opposite party for simultaneous trial of the Demra PS Case No. 45(5) 89 with the Sessions Case No. 162 of 1989 arising out of Demra PS Case No. 45 (5) 89 and with that end in view withdrew the case from the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka to his own file. 

 4. Mr. Khan Saifur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner in support of the rule, made submission on 3 counts : His first ground is that subsequent case being Demra PS Case No. 49(5) 89 is exclusively triable by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Dhaka and not by any court of Sessions by the mandate of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the provision of section 526(B) CrPC does not authorise the learned Sessions Judge and confer upon him the trial ability of the case and in that view of the matter the learned Sessions Judge erred in law in passing the impugned order. The learned Advocate referred to section 526B(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure which runs as follows: 

 "Where it is made to appear to a Sessions Judge that an order under this section is expedient for the ends of justice he may" order that any particular case be transferred from one Criminal Court to another Criminal Court in his Sessions Division." 

 5. By way of elucidating his point the learned Advocate submits that all the sections for which charge sheet has been submitted in the Demra PS Case No. 49(5) 89 are exclusively triable by the Court of Magistrate and the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate except one under section 307 PC, which though triable by the Sessions Judge there appears to be no ingredient of the offence justifying submission of charge sheet under the said section and in that view of the matter the jurisdiction vested in the Magistrate should not have been divested by the Higher Court. 

 6. Mr. A Baset Majumder, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties, submits that the provision of law authorising the Sessions Judge to transfer a case from one Criminal Court to another Criminal- Court under the provision of section 339B(1) of the Code does not preclude the Sessions Judge from assuming jurisdiction of withdrawing the case from the court of Magistrate or Metropolitan Magistrate, as the case may be, to his own me and or to try the same himself or to send it for trial to the court of sessions who is vested with the jurisdiction of trying all types of criminal cases. Mr. Majumder submits that the charge-sheet having been submitted under section 307 of the Penal Code the case is concurrently triable by the court of Metropolitan Magistrate and also by the Sessions Judge and whether there is any ingredient of the offence under section 307 is not the matter for consideration and determination at this stage but could be seen only at the time of trial of the case. Mr. Baset Majumder further submits that the case being a counter case has rightly been withdrawn for its trial simultaneously with the other case pending before the Additional Sessions Judge. 

 7. The relevant laws on the point and the judicial pronouncements with regard to transfer of cases from the Court or Magistrate to the Court of Sessions, which is admittedly a court of higher jurisdiction and status in Criminal matters favor the view that the Sessions Judge has always the power and jurisdiction to withdraw the case from the court of Magistrate to his own me and try the case himself or send it for trial to the Additional Court of Sessions having jurisdiction and competency to try such cases, if it is found expedient for the ends of justice, particularly when a case can be said to be a counter case of the other and as such required to be tried simultaneously with a case exclusively triable by the Court of Sessions. We, therefore, do not find any substance in the first point urged by the learned Advocate for the petitioner. 

 8. It is next submitted by Mr. Khan Saifur Rahman that consequent on the filing of a petition by Mst. Aleya Begum, the complainant of Demra PS Case No. 49(5) 89 before the Sessions Judge, Narayangonj being Misc. Case No. 2393 of 1989 the learned Sessions Judge by his order dated 20.11.89 sent back the case to the, Court of Magistrate for trial on the ground that the said case was not triable by the Court of Sessions. In the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the opposite party it is stated that the record was sent to the Sessions Judge in connection with bail application at the instance of the present petitioners who are accused in the case being Demra PS Case No. 49(5) 89 and the record having been found tampered with and thereafter corrected the learned Sessions Judge on receipt of the same sent back the case to the Court of Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka for trial as the Misc. Case (Transfer) was not found ready for want of service of notice for non-filing of talabana and therefore, the prayer for transfer of the case was rejected on 20.11.89. Mr. Khan Saifur Rahman submits that the impugned order tantamount to a review of the earlier order dated 20.11.89 passed in Criminal Misc. Case No. 2393 of 1989 and as the matter has already been decided earlier, the learned Sessions Judge committed error in entertaining a second petition for withdrawing the case from the file of the Metropolitan Magistrate and in that view of the matter the impugned order cannot be sustained. 

 9. Mr. A. Baset Majumder in reply submits that since the order was not passed on merit earlier there was no absence of jurisdiction for the Sessions Judge to entertain the application for transfer and passing appropriate order for the ends of justice. On perusal of the records we find that the order previously passed by the learned Sessions Judge was in a Misc. Case and that too, was not on merit and, therefore, the learned Sessions Judge was not ceased of the jurisdiction to entertain a petition for transfer and passing necessary order. 

 10. The next ground taken by Mr. Khan Saifur Rahman is that the place of occurrence and the time of occurrence and the incident of the earlier case and the subsequent case could not be said to be the counter case of the earlier one and hence there is no requirement for holding simultaneous trial of the two cases, rather it would be more expedient for the ends of justice to allow the respective courts to try the cases having jurisdiction over the same. The learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party, by way of refuting the arguments of the learned Advocate for petitioners, submits that the place and time of occurrence of the two cases are almost the same and, moreover, some of the accused for one case are witnesses in the other and vice versa and for that matter the case being Demra PS Case No. 49(5) 89 for all practical purposes is the counter case of the earlier case being Demra PS Case No. 45(5) 89 and, therefore, in all fairness both the cases are required to be tried simultaneously by the same court in order to avoid conflicting decisions. The learned Advocate further submits that there is no bar and there is also no question of prejudice in holding trial by the superior court in respect of the case which is normally triable by the Court of Magistrate when it becomes necessary for holding trial of such a case which is a counter case of the other case exclusively triable by the Court of Sessions. 

 11. In order to appreciate the point raised by the learned Advocate of both the sides a little bit of background of both the cases will be necessary. Let us now first give herein below the short facts of Sessions Case No. 162 of 1989 arising out of the Demra PS Case No. 49(5) 89 now pending before the Additional Sessions Judge, Dhaka, the facts are as follows: 

 13. On the basis of the said FIR Demra PS Case No. 45(5)89 was started and the police after investigation submitted charge sheet against Afsar Karim under sections 148/149/302 of the Penal Code. 

 14. Three days after the lodging of the above FIR by Mujibur Rahman the opposite party No. 1 Mst. Aleya Begum, daughter of Afsar Karim, filed a petition of complaint before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, alleging that about 800/900 miscreants being armed in order to kill her father Afsar Karim, and her relations, some of them set fire to the surrounding houses and started looting. The miscreants also attacked the house of Afsar Karim, threw brick bats, started firing and there was an attempt to kill the informant's father Afsar Karim. It was also stated that the accused petitioner No. 1 started a false case against her father Afsar Karim and got her father arrested, out of fear the complainant could not go to the police station and thus some delay was caused in lodging the petition of complaint. The case having been referred to the police station the complaint petition was treated as FIR and the case being Demra PS Case No; 49(5) 89 was started. The police after completion of investigation submitted charge sheet under sections 148/149/302/420/380/109 of the Penal Code and the said case now pending before the Metropolitan Magistrate is sought to be transferred there from to the Court of Sessions. 

 15. The facts of both the cases as disclosed from the FIR and charge-sheet are stated above. We have taken into consideration and have, already expressed our view with regard to the first and second points urged by the learned Advocate for the petitioner. Let us take up now the third point urged by Mr. Khan Saifur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner. This point deserves some elaboration and consideration in the light of the facts of the two cases stated above. Mr. Khan Saifur Rahman submits that the order passed by the Sessions Judge withdrawing the case from the file of Metropolitan Magistrate to his own file for the purpose of holding trial simultaneously with the sessions case pending before the Additional Sessions Judge, and Court, Dhaka cannot be sustained in view of the fact that the case pending before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate being Demra PS Case No. 49(5) 89 cannot be said to be a counter case of the Sessions Case No. 162 of 1989 arising out of Demra PS Case No. 45(5)89. Reading out the FIR and charge sheet of the respective cases the learned Advocate submits that the time, place and manner of occurrence of the two cases are different and distinct and though the accused Afsar Karim of Demra PS Case No. 45(5)89 is a witness in the other case the subsequent case was filed not by him but"' by his daughter Mst. Aleya Begum who is not connected in the previous case in any way. Mr. Khan submits that the subsequent case may be a case in reprisal of the other case but not a counter case and hence does not call for holding its trial with the other" case which is ready for trial in Court of Sessions: 

 16. Mr. A. Baset Majumder submits that one is the counter case of another as the time, place and manner of occurrence of both the two cases are almost the same and some of the accused in one case are the witnesses in another case. Relying on the decisions of the High Court Division and the Appellate Division on the point, Mr. Baset Majumder, the learned Advocate for the opposite party, contends that the learned Sessions Judge had not committed any illegality or even irregularity in withdrawing the case from the Court of Metropolitan Magistrate for its trial along with the Session Case No. 62 of 1989 pending for trial in the second court of Additional Sessions Judge, Dhaka, as it is deemed by him expedient for the ends of Justice. Mr. Khan Saifur Rahman does not dispute the principle laid down in the cited cases for holding simultaneous trial by the same court if it relates to a case and counter case. Mr. Khan Saifur Rahman's endeavour was to take a distinction because of the distinguishing features of the present two cases and he' strenuously argued that in the present cases occurrence is not the same and two cases are different so far it relates to time, place and manner of occurrence and therefore it is neither expedient nor even necessary for holding the trial of the said two cases simultaneously by the same court. Though the Code of Criminal Procedure is silent with regard to the procedure to be adopted in the trial or a counter case arising out of the same occurrence and it has not been laid down anywhere in the Code as an absolute rule that all charges or counter charges must be tried by the same court, generally a court should be allowed to try the cases if they are so competent to do so, but in a series of judicial pronouncements of the superior courts of the subcontinent it has been laid down that the case and counter case should be heard simultaneously by the same court but the only requirement is that record of each case should be kept distinct and each must be decided on its own merit. The learned Sessions Judge on perusal of the record found that the case which was sought to be withdrawn by him from the court of Magistrate was the counter case of another which was already found to be pending before the Additional Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka, and as such he passed the order for the withdrawal of the case from the court below so as to pave the way for simultaneous trial by the same court. The learned Sessions Judge in passing such order relied on the case of Shamsul Huq alias Shamsu and others Vs. The State reported in 38 DLR (AD) 75 wherein it is observed: 

 "Trial of cross cases" which arise from the same incident, by the same court enables it to better appreciate the evidence and circumstances which are described by parties in conflicting manners. By such trial the court gets the picture and arrives at correct decision avoiding conflicting findings which are likely to occur if separate courts held the trials. Though no express provision of law requires trial of cross-cases by the same court, practice and experience of over a century dictate such trial for arriving at correct determination of disputed facts, This is all the more necessary to save the accused from being prejudiced in their defence." 

 17. The view taken in the case is in line with the expressions in a series of cases decided by the superior courts of the sub-continent and also in the case reported in 8 DLR 447, 13 DLR 417 and 21 DLR 958. 

 18. In the case reported in PLD 1971 (SC) 713 it is observed as follows: 

 "The Code of Criminal Procedure is silent with regard to the procedure to be adopted in the trial of counter cases arising out of the same occurrence. It has not been laid down anywhere in the Code as an absolute rule that all charges and counter charges must be ---- 

 19. The principle is now well settled that if any case is found to be a counter case of another then it is desirable that both the cases are to be tried simultaneously one after another by the same court for the ends of justice. Therefore, it is to be determined first as to whether in the Cases sought to be tried simultaneously with the other cases referred to above it is found that the case which arose out of the same occurrence or incident or when the time, place and manner of occurrence are the same and similar and the witnesses of one case is the accused in another case and vice versa it could be said that one case is the counter case of another. Besides this; the learned Advocates appearing for the petitioner as well as for the opposite parties have not been able to lay their hands on any provision of law or decision giving out the criteria determining a case as the counter case of the other. Mr. A Baset Majumder has referred to the case of Alauddin Molla and others Vs. The State reported in 42 DLR (AD) 281, relevant page 285. Though in the said case the prayer for simultaneous trial was not allowed on the ground that there was laches on the part of the petitioner in making a prayer to that effect but it supports the view taken and principle laid down in 13 DLR (Dhaka) 414 wherein it is held that a case and counter case in respect of the same occurrence should be tried simultaneously by the same judge keeping the records of the two cases distinct and separate. In the case reported in 42 DLR (AD) 281 relevant (285) it is further observed that even in cases where one is not the counter case of another in respect of time, place and manner of occurrence but it may, be possible to argue that two cases are, such that simultaneous trial by the same court will be necessary for the interest of justice. 

 20. In the case of Shahed Ali and others Vs. The State reported in 13 DLR 414 it was held: 

 "Where there is a case and counter case in respect of the same occurrence it is desirable that they should be tried by the same Judge yet, the records of each case should be kept-distinct and separate. The evidence on record of one case cannot be used in connection with the other case." 

 21. Thus we find 'that the main criteria to decide whether one case is a counter case of another is the occurrence. In the present case as we have already found that in the case filed by Mujibur Rahmanthe place of occurrence has been given as Dhaka-Narayangonj Road and also the place near the house of Haji Afsar Karim. In the other case bearing Case No. 49(5) 89 the place of occurrence has been given as the house of complainant Mst. Aleya Begum as well as it spoke about the attack on house of Afsar Karim who is an accused No. 1 in other case. Time of occurrence as given in the earlier case is 8-00 PM and the other case from the First Information Report and also from the charge sheet time of occurrence appears to be 8-00/9-00 PM. It is also found from the records of both the cases that the accused No. 1 Afsar Karim in Demra PS Case No. 45(5) 89 and accused No. 2 Tajul Islam are witnesses in other case being Demra PS Case No. 49(5) 89 and the witnesses Mr. Nizamuddin and Md. Lutfur Rahman in the earlier case are accused in the subsequent case. Mr. Khan Saifur Rahman has made efforts to make out a distinction between the two cases so far it relates to the place of occurrence and time of occurrence and involvement of the accused persons either as accused or witnesses but on a careful scrutiny of-both the cases and the charge sheet and other materials on record we find it difficult to say at the moment that the two cases are distinctly separate and one is not at all connected with the other far the time of occurrence, place of occurrence and the accused and witnesses are concerned. Since it is found that over the occurrence there are two conflicting versions of the respective parties the August 18th, 1991 learned Sessions Judge seemed to have committed no illegality-or even irregularity in holding that one case is the counter case of another and in that view of the matter passing the order for withdrawal of the case from the Metropolitan Magistrate to his own court for the purpose of sending it to the court for holding simultaneous trial with the case which is pending before the Additional Sessions Judge, Second Court, Dhaka, by such trial the court will get opportunity for looking to all the aspects of both the cases which is necessary for arriving at a correct decision and avoid conflicting findings which are likely to occur if trial is held separately. Furthermore, if one case appears to be the counter case of the other the second case which is not exactly the same, the order; if any be made for holding trial simultaneously by the same court, no question of prejudice will arise as in the present case the Court of Sessions is admittedly the higher court to that of the Court of Metropolitan Magistrate. 

 22. In view of the above, we find the order of the learned Sessions Judge withdrawing the case being Demra PS Case No. 49(5) 89' from the Court of Magistrate to his own court so that the trial could be held simultaneously with the other case by the Additional Sessions Judge, does not suffer from infirmities and hence we do not find ground for interference.
